successors.note: The state was a federal state of the German Empire from 1871 and ended in November 1918 (see the dissolve event); the Weimar Republic took over its land (Free State of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach). The German Empire was its overlord, not its successor, so it is no longer listed here (fx-53 D01, was the 1871 dissolve into german-empire; same change as fx-46 R122 for Bavaria); the hierarchy.csv row grand-duchy-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator.

ledger.note: 1806: the duchies of Saxe-Weimar and Saxe-Eisenach, one duke since 1741, enter the Confederation of the Rhine. 'Duke Charles Augustus joined the Confederation of the Rhine on 15 December 1806' to avoid deposition; 'Saxe-Weimar and Saxe-Eisenach came under one ruler' in 1741. Cliopatria starts the row in 1806; the page's 'Established' date is the merger of 20 September 1809 (see the rename event).

region.text: Weimar and Eisenach under Duke Charles Augustus

ledger.note: 4 August 1807: Napoleon takes Blankenhain from Saxe-Weimar. 'On 4 August 1807 Napoleon attached the Saxe-Weimar territory of Blankenhain' to the Principality of Erfurt, which he declared 'directly subordinate to himself as an imperial state domain'.

20 September 1809: Weimar and Eisenach are merged into the Duchy of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach. 'The two duchies officially merged into the Duchy of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach, with separate districts around Weimar and Eisenach.'
1815: the Congress of Vienna raises the duchy to a grand duchy. 'The Congress of Vienna raised the state to a grand duchy' and it joined the German Confederation.

1815: the Neustadt district comes to Weimar. 'In the east, it gained most of the Neustädter Kreis' from the Kingdom of Saxony; the Kingdom of Saxony page says the Thuringian and Neustadt circles were 'annexed by Prussia' and 'most of the Neustadt Circle was re-ceded to Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach by Prussia', so Prussia is the giver (the Saxony dossier records the loss against Prussia). The pages give no month.

ledger.note: 1815: the Eisenacher Oberland is added in the west. 'The Eisenacher Oberland was created from adjacent former parts of Hesse-Kassel' and territories of the Princely Abbey of Fulda; the Fulda page says Fulda went to the Electorate of Hesse in 1815 and was occupied by Prussia from 1815 and says nothing of Weimar. The Fulda share has no separate region here.

ledger.note: September 1815: Blankenhain and southern and eastern Erfurt lands pass from Prussia to Weimar. 'Erfurt was restored to Prussia on 21 June 1815'; 'some southern and eastern parts of Erfurter lands joined Blankenhain in being transferred to the Grand Duchy of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach the following September' (the year is read from the June 1815 restoration). The Weimar page says it received 'most of the Principality of Erfurt', 'Blankenhain and Kranichfeld'; the Erfurt page keeps the city with Prussia as a district capital of the Province of Saxony.

ledger.note: 9 November 1918: the grand duke abdicates. 'William Ernest abdicated the throne on 9 November 1918, thereby ending the monarchy in the state'; 'The grand duchy came to an end in the German Revolution of 1918-19 with the other monarchies of the German Empire'; 'It continued as the Free State of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach, until 1920'. In 1871 it 'joined the new German Empire as a constituent state' (infobox 'Federal State of the German Empire (1871-1918)'). Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Prussia won; Hesse-Kassel was incorporated into Prussia's Province of Hesse-Nassau and the grand duchy joined the North German Confederation.
wars.note: The page names no battle in the grand duchy and no territorial change for Weimar, so there is no zone; the grand duchy's side is not stated on the page.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary; the Napoleonic-era lands include exclaves (Blankenhain lost 1807, the Ilmenau, Allstedt, Oldisleben and Ostheim exclaves).

Treaty borders of the Vienna settlement of 1815; the exclaves of Ilmenau, Allstedt, Oldisleben and Ostheim stay as small enclaves. 1872-1918 (fx-53): the dossier records no frontier change after 1871; the state keeps its 1870 outline as a federal state of the German Empire.

notes: Five pages used (the Neustadt an der Orla and Fulda Abbey pages were thin). Cliopatria staging does not match the page: the Vienna gains (Neustadt district in the east, Eisenacher Oberland in the west, Blankenhain and Erfurt lands) are dated 1815, while the shapes add the west in 1820 and the east in 1828 and then shrink in 1866; the corrections give the 1868 shape (3,610 km2, equal to the 3,595 km2 of the 1895 district areas) for 1815-1865. The 1807-1808 shape holds only the Eisenach side. Not settled: the exact month of the Vienna transfers; the Fulda share of the Eisenacher Oberland (the Fulda page names only Hesse); whether the Principality of Erfurt (Prussian from the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss of 25 February 1803, French from the capitulation of 16 October 1806, an imperial state domain from 4 August 1807, restored to Prussia on 21 June 1815) needs a dossier of its own (Blankenhain counterpart); the Weimar page's 'most of the Principality of Erfurt' against the Erfurt page's 'some southern and eastern parts'; Cliopatria's 1828 shape reaching Altenburg and Gera. The Neustadt gain is recorded against Prussia (the Saxony and Weimar pages together), while the Weimar page names Saxony. Coordinates used for places the gazetteer lacks: Blankenhain, Neustadt an der Orla, Dermbach, Vacha, Eisenach. 1809 merger and 1815 elevation are `rename` events (colour continues). The dossier ends in 1871 as the sibling German states do, the grand duchy lasting to 9 November 1918. REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (grand-duchy-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row grand-duchy-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator.
